How to Earn 54% ROI in St. Clair County Tax Lien Sales

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Investing in St. Clair County’s tax lien sales offers an excellent opportunity to earn up to 54% returns. Each year, the county hosts an auction to recover unpaid property taxes, allowing investors to purchase tax lien certificates and earn significant interest. This can be a highly profitable way to grow your investments with relatively low entry costs, especially when compared to traditional investment avenues.

What Are Tax Lien Certificates?

A tax lien certificate is issued on properties with unpaid taxes, giving investors the right to pay the delinquent taxes in exchange for earning interest. When you buy a tax lien, you hold a claim on the property. The property owner must pay back the overdue taxes along with interest to clear the lien. If the owner fails to redeem the lien within the redemption period, the investor can begin foreclosure proceedings to acquire the property.

Example:
If you purchase a tax lien at 6%, you earn this interest every six months until the lien is redeemed. If the lien remains unpaid over the course of two to three years, the return can be substantial.

Outcome:
Should the owner fail to pay the lien within the 24-30-month redemption period, the investor can file for a tax deed and acquire the property for the cost of back taxes and related fees.

Important Details for St. Clair County Tax Lien Sales

Steps to Start Investing in St. Clair County Tax Liens

1. Research Local Laws

Familiarize yourself with Illinois tax lien laws, particularly Chapter 35 of the Illinois State Statutes. Understanding the redemption period, foreclosure process, and interest rates is crucial to making informed decisions.

2. Visit the St. Clair County Treasurer’s Website

The St. Clair County Treasurer’s Office provides detailed information about the auction process, including sale schedules, registration, and parcel inquiries. Visit the site to access relevant forms and instructions.

3. Check the Auction Site

St. Clair County holds its tax lien auctions both in-person and online through GovEase. You can register and bid online or attend the auction at the St. Clair County Building in Belleville. For more information, visit the Auction Site.

4. Review Sale Information

Before participating, make sure to review the tax sale packet and delinquent tax lists. These are typically available a few weeks before the auction, giving you time to research specific properties.

5. Contact the Treasurer’s Office

For any questions about the auction or tax lien certificates, contact the St. Clair County Treasurer’s Office at (618) 825-2707 or email at treasurer@co.st-clair.il.us. It’s essential to clarify any doubts before the auction date.

Pro Tips for Successful Tax Lien Investing

  1. Register Early: The registration deadline is October, and a $500 deposit is required. Early registration ensures you have enough time to prepare.
  2. Single Bidder Rule: Be aware of the single bidder rule to avoid violations that could lead to the cancellation of your bids or future participation bans.
  3. Participate in Person: Although online bidding is available, you must attend in person to complete initial registration. This also gives you a chance to better understand the auction process.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. When is the next tax sale?

The next tax sale in St. Clair County is scheduled for November 4, 2024, at 9:00 a.m.

2. How do I register for the tax sale?

Register by October 18, 2024, by submitting a $500 registration fee to the St. Clair County Treasurer’s Office. You can find registration forms and instructions on their website.

3. What if the property owner doesn’t redeem the lien?

If the property owner does not pay the delinquent taxes within the 24 to 30-month redemption period, you can petition the court for a tax deed and acquire ownership of the property.

4. Can I participate online?

Yes, St. Clair County offers online bidding through GovEase. You can register, bid, and manage your account online.

5. How does the bidding process work?

The auction starts at 9% interest, and the interest rate is bid down. The investor who accepts the lowest interest rate wins the lien.
